page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-8 is an arm64-based general-purpose server instance powered by an 8-core Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. The instance is equipped with 32 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks place the t2a-standard-8 in the middle tier for multi-core operations, software compilation, and database tasks. It achieves a multi-core Geekbench score of 6000.0 and a static web serving throughput of 10.09 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1073.0 and a weak Passmark CPU score of 6205.54. Memory performance is mixed, with high cached read bandwidth at 563.91 GB/sec but a lower Passmark memory score.

The ARM architecture lacks x86-specific instruction sets like AVX or AMX, which impacts vector and matrix math performance. This is reflected in poor LLM text generation speeds of 32.29 tokens/sec and weak single-threaded bzip3 decompression. The instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for scale-out workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading. It is best suited for static web serving, Redis caching, software compilation, and general-purpose multi-threaded application hosting.

It is configured with 32 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and contains no local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmarks indicate average multi-core performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 6000.0 and a static web serving throughput of 10.09 GB/sec. However, single-core performance and cryptographic operations are weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1073.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 6205.54. Lacking AVX and AMX instruction sets, this instance is not suited for heavy vector math or LLM inference. It offers a qualitatively cost-efficient profile for scale-out workloads, making it highly suitable for web serving, Redis caching, software compilation, and multi-threaded application hosting.
